overview: SSC CGL is the Staff Selection Commission's flagship exam for **Group B and Group C posts** across central government ministries and departments — from Assistant Section Officer and Income Tax Inspector to Auditor and Tax Assistant. No interview, two computer-based stages, and roughly 12,000+ appointments in a good year. The exam rewards **speed + accuracy on a fixed syllabus**: the same ~19 Quant topics, 20 Reasoning types, 12 English areas and a wide GA canvas appear every single year, which is exactly why smart preparation (shortcuts + topic tests + full mocks) beats generic study. **Tier 1 only shortlists you — final selection comes from Tier 2**, so your prep target is a Tier 2 score out of 390, not just a Tier 1 cutoff.

stages.notes: Session-I lasts **135 minutes**: Section-I (Maths + Reasoning) 60 min, Section-II (English + GA) 60 min, and Section-III Module-I Computer Knowledge 15 min (qualifying). Session-II is the **15-minute DEST** — a data-entry speed test (2000 key depressions in 15 min, also qualifying). The paper carries **450 raw marks**, but Computer's 60 marks are qualifying only, so merit is out of **390** (Maths 90 + Reasoning 90 + English 135 + GA 75). **Paper 2 (Statistics, 100Q × 2 = 200, 2 hours)** is only for JSO aspirants. Section-wise qualifying minimums apply in Paper 1.

selectionProcess: **Tier 1 (screening) → Tier 2 Paper 1 (merit) → Document Verification → Allotment.** Tier 1 rank only decides who sits Tier 2. Tier 2 Paper 1 score (out of 390, normalised) is the merit list. The Computer Knowledge module and DEST are qualifying hurdles inside Tier 2 — you must clear them but their marks don't count. JSO aspirants additionally need Paper 2 (Statistics). There is **no interview** for any CGL post.
normalization: Because Tier 1 (and Tier 2) run in many shifts with different question papers, SSC **normalises scores across shifts** before declaring results: raw scores are statistically adjusted using the mean and standard deviation of all candidates in each shift, so a harder shift isn't a penalty. Practical consequences: (1) never compare raw marks across shifts or years; (2) in the exam, maximise attempts where *your* shift's paper is soft; (3) don't panic if your raw score looks below the cutoff — your normalised score is what counts.

faqs.q: Is Tier 1 marks counted in the final selection?
faqs.a: No. Tier 1 is only a screening stage — its score decides who reaches Tier 2. The final merit list is drawn from **Tier 2 Paper 1 (out of 390)**. A mediocre Tier 1 with qualification is as good as a top Tier 1 score.

faqs.q: What is the negative marking in SSC CGL?
faqs.a: Tier 1: **−0.50** per wrong answer. Tier 2 Paper 1: **−1** per wrong answer (each correct answer carries +3 in Tier 2 vs +2 in Tier 1). Unanswered questions cost nothing.

faqs.q: Is there any limit on the number of attempts?
faqs.a: No attempt limit exists — you can apply every year until you cross the age limit for the posts you're targeting (18–27 for most, up to 32 for JSO, plus category relaxations).

faqs.q: How does normalisation work across shifts?
faqs.a: SSC statistically adjusts raw scores using each shift's mean and standard deviation so that candidates in harder shifts aren't disadvantaged. This is why cutoffs refer to **normalised** scores and why raw marks across shifts aren't comparable.

faqs.q: Are calculators or mobile phones allowed?
faqs.a: No. No calculator, smartwatch, or electronic device is allowed in the exam hall. Rough work is done on sheets provided at the centre. Mental-maths speed (tables to 20, squares to 40, cubes to 20, fraction–percentage equivalents) is a scored skill — build it.

faqs.q: Is there a sectional cutoff or sectional time limit?
faqs.a: Tier 1 has **no sectional cutoff**, but candidates in the 2026 shifts reported a **15-minute locked timer for each of the four sections** (60 minutes total), so you cannot go back to a section once it locks. Tier 2 Paper 1 has module timing (60 min for Maths+Reasoning, 60 min for English+GA, 15 min Computer) and section-wise qualifying minimums.

faqs.q: What is DEST and who needs it?
faqs.a: Data Entry Speed Test — a qualifying Tier 2 module where you must type about **2000 key depressions in 15 minutes**. All posts require it; marks don't count in merit. Practice on a standard keyboard if you type on a phone all day.

faqs.q: Is the Computer Knowledge module difficult?
faqs.a: It's 20 questions, 15 minutes, **qualifying only** — basic computer fundamentals, MS Office, internet/email, networking and cyber-security awareness. The mock tests and notes on this site cover the whole module.

faqs.q: Which posts are considered the best in CGL?
faqs.a: By pay and profile: **AAO** (Level 8) > **ASO in CSS / Income Tax Inspector / CBDT-CBIC Inspectors / SI CBI** (Level 7) > JSO (Level 6) > Auditor/Accountant (Level 5) > Tax Assistant (Level 4). 'Best' depends on posting city, field vs desk work, and transfer frequency — Inspector posts get more field duty; CSS ASO is Delhi-desk heavy.

faqs.q: Can I crack CGL in 3–4 months of preparation?
faqs.a: Yes — a large share of selections every year come from 3–5 month focused preps, especially with a Quant/Reasoning base. The winning pattern: **topic notes + shortcut drills first, then topic tests, then full mocks every 2–3 days** with a mistakes notebook. The 60-minute Tier 1 format punishes slow calculation more than missing knowledge.

faqs.q: What score should I target to be safe?
faqs.a: Use the [score calculator](/ssc-cgl/score-calculator/) with recent cutoffs: for Tier 1 qualification aim **150+ / 200** (UR), and for a realistic final selection aim a Tier 2 merit score around **330+/390** for popular posts — higher (340+) for AAO/ASO-grade posts in high-vacancy years.

faqs.q: When and where is the Tier 1 admit card released?
faqs.a: Roughly **4 days before your exam shift**, on the regional SSC website (not the main ssc.gov.in) — the region depends on where you applied from. You'll also get an SMS/email with the download link.

faqs.q: What documents are needed at the exam centre?
faqs.a: Admit card printout + **original photo ID** (Aadhaar preferred) + two recent passport photos. Check the admit card's instructions — items like wallets, pens in branded covers, and jewellery can be barred at some centres.

faqs.q: Is there any interview in SSC CGL?
faqs.a: No. CGL has had **no interview** since 2016 — selection is purely the written Tier 2 merit plus document verification.

faqs.q: Can candidates from any state apply for any SSC region?
faqs.a: You choose a region while applying and your exam centres fall within that region. Choose based on where you can realistically travel — centre city options appear in the application form.

documents: At Document Verification you need: **matriculation certificate** (DOB proof), **bachelor's degree marksheets + certificate**, **category certificate** (OBC/EWS/SC/ST in the central-government format, current validity year), **PwD/ESM certificate** if applicable, photo ID (Aadhaar/PAN/passport), recent passport photographs, and the **undertaking/options form** for post preference. Name mismatches between documents are the #1 DV headache — carry a gazette affidavit or supporting proof if your name spellings differ. OBC candidates: the certificate must be in the central OBC format with the correct financial-year issue date, or your category is switched to UR on the spot.
